newsitem.title: ITALY: Mafioso says Italy's Andreotti met godfather Riina.
newsitem.headline: Mafioso says Italy's Andreotti met godfather Riina.

text.p: The brother of an accused Mafia killer told a court on Monday that former Italian Prime Minister Giulio Andreotti had met "boss of bosses" Salvatore Riina in the late 1980s while the organised crime chief was on the run.

Enzo Brusca, arrested last year with his brother Giovanni, was testifying at the trial of the seven-times former premier, who is accused of protecting the Mafia while he held various public offices in his long career.

"It is true that there was a meeting between 'Toto' Riina and Giulio Andreotti," Brusca told the court in Rome's high-security Rebbibia jail, adding he had heard of the meeting from his brother Emmanuele, another alleged Mafioso.
Andreotti, a life senator whose trial began in 1994, denies the charges, saying they are part of an elaborate Mafia plot to punish him for crackdowns on organised crime by governments he headed.
Enzo Brusca admitted that he had lied to investigators when he said previously that Riina's former bodyguard Balduccio Di Maggio had told him of the alleged 1987 meeting between Riina and Andreotti.
Andreotti told reporters the fact that Enzo Brusca had admitted he lied about where he had heard of the alleged meeting proved his testimony could not be trusted.
Di Maggio says Andreotti and Riina met secretly in the Sicilian capital, Palermo, and exchanged a kiss of respect. The alleged meeting is the key part of the prosecution's case against Andreotti.
Riina, known as "The Beast," was arrested in 1993 after nearly a quarter of a century on the run.
Giovanni Brusca was due to appear in court later on Monday.
In his own trial on murder charges last January, Giovanni Brusca accused Andreotti of using his power to influence the outcome of Mafia trials.
